page: Microsoft Azure E64-32as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Easv7 series, configured with constrained core counts to maximize memory-per-core density. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features 512.0 GB of system memory, delivering a high ratio of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16), VAES, and SHA extensions. The instance includes no local storage and does not bundle dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on remote Azure storage volumes.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-thread execution and instruction execution capabilities. The AMD EPYC 9V45 cores deliver top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng (3,117.49) and PassMark CPU metrics (57,541.16 overall, with strong encryption and extended instruction results). Single-threaded data compression is equally fast, registering 41.32 GB/sec in gzip and 18.19 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks remain within average tier parameters at 100.91 GB/sec for reads and 67.8 GB/sec for writes. CPU-driven inference tasks on lightweight models show strong throughput, while large 70B parameter models remain constrained by CPU execution bounds.

With its 1:16 vCPU-to-memory distribution, the E64-32as_v7 provides qualitative cost efficiency for software environments licensed per core that demand massive memory footprints. Tradeoffs include reliance on network-attached storage due to the absence of local disks, and average multi-core throughput relative to full-socket allocations. The instance is specifically suited for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory relational databases, Redis caching clusters, enterprise ERP platforms, and memory-heavy analytics processing.
